children: By Callum Keown
The global bond selloff is reaching dangerous levels, and it's threatening the stock market.
The 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.447% early Thursday-its highest level since 2004, while the 10-year yield is at its highest since 2007. Those stats are slightly terrifying.
Stocks are braced for another difficult day and potentially a difficult end to the year. Energy is the only bright spot, and that's as oil prices are rising.

The market is increasingly confident of another rate increase in October-the odds rose to 75% on CME's FedWatch tool early Thursday. New York Fed President John Williams said it was "reasonable" to expect another hike this year at a conference in London. But by the time the U.S. woke up, the market was firmly pricing in two hikes.

Highflying tech stocks typically get hit amid higher rate expectations, and Thursday looks no different. You wouldn't know that Meta had just unveiled a potentially pivotal AI device to support its popular Muse AI agent.
Maybe the bond pressure will break the impasse between the U.S. and Iran-if it doesn't it might break the stock market.

🏦 Treasury yields surged to highest levels in two decades

The yield on the five-year Treasury closed at the highest level since 2007, just under 5%, and the yields on the 10- and 30-Year Treasuries all hit 52-week highs to levels reached about two decades ago, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Many pointed to a 5-year auction that many described as "failed" because of weak demand.
🌍 The Trump-Xi summit: What investors are watching

Both President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping will focus on preserving stability when they meet today. Investors are focused on the fate of a fragile detente that expires Nov. 10, plus tariff reductions, potential deals on agriculture, energy, and artificial intelligence, and signs of cooperation on AI and the war in Iran.
🍽? CEOs flock to state dinner. One isn't on the list.

President Trump is hosting CEOs and other luminaries at a state dinner for China's visiting Xi Jinping tonight, with a guest list that includes General Motors' Mary Barra, Tesla's Elon Musk, and Nvidia's Jensen Huang, among others. Ford's Jim Farley is notably not on the list. Read more here.
🍟 McDonald's to spend $8.5 billion to accelerate changes

McDonald's sees chicken and beverages as two of its biggest opportunities to gain market share. The restaurant giant outlined some of its plans during an investor day, including an $8.5 billion strategy to help franchisees accelerate reaching its profitability goals. Read more about it here.
🏰 Disney is raising streaming bundle prices amid AI hoopla

Walt Disney is following Netflix and Comcast's Peacock in raising the prices for some of its streaming bundles as it invests in content. The move, which raises some prices by as much as 10%, comes amid this week's buzz about how AI agents will affect companies that rely on so-called "consumer inertia" with subscription platforms.
